Date April 4th 1939
Subject (in full) Yaroslav Formanek and Karel Tulka
Made by D. S. Orsiannikoff. Forwarded by J. M. Swiero A. B. (Pol)
Sir,
With reference to the attached file, inquiries made at
local hotels and boarding houses have failed to locate Yaroslav
Formanek and Karel Tulka. It is reported they have left Shanghai.
V Orsiannikoff.
D. S.
A/D.C.I.

A. A. C. I.,

The following information was
received by me through private official sources:-

Memo re Jaroslav Formanek and
Karel Tulka.

Letter from Leo Schuurmaecker,
Czechoslovak Consul at Manila to
Governor Philippine Islands dated
at Manila, January 31, 1929:-

"Jaroslav Formanek, a Czechoslovak
"citizen, arrived at Manila 2 weeks
"ago (abt. Jan. 17) and in the meantime
"this Consulate received a warning
"from the Minister of Foreign Affairs
"at Prague, and from the Czechoslovak
"Consulate at Bombay, to the effect
"that Jaroslav Formanek staged a
"fake boxing match at Bombay,
"while here (Manila) he pretends
"to be a reporter for Czechoslovak
"newspapers, at the same time solicit-
"ing funds from different people
"in the community. In view of the
"aforesaid, he is not considered a
"desirable visitor to these Islands and,
"for the reasons stated, this office
"shall greatly appreciate it if, through

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. I. D. REGISTRY
No. I. O. D. 91
Date 15: 3: 29

SECRET

H. B. M. Consulate-General,
Shanghai.
14th. March, 1929.

My dear Alers,

With reference to your Memo No. I.O.D 81 dated
the 6th. of March, 1929, I made enquiries from India by
telegram about Jaroslav-Formanek and have just received
a reply to the effect that this individual and Karel Tulka,
Austrian Czecho-Slovakians, applied in May 1928 to the
Passport Control Officer in Prague for visas to India.
They described themselves as boxers and journalists re-
presenting the Press Service Agency of Prague, a weekly
illustrated paper published in Prague and a sporting
paper entitled the "Ring". As nothing was known against
them no objection was raised to the grant of a visa. They
arrived in Bombay on the 15th. of September, 1928, and
stated that they are touring the world. In Bombay they
maintained themselves by giving pugilistic exhibitions.
Further enquiries are being made in India, the result of
which will be communicated to you.

Yours sincerely,
G. H. A. Hall

R. C. Alers, Esq.,
Assistant Commissioner of Police,
Criminal Investigation Department,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
SHANGHAI.

日期 1929年3月15日

秘密

英国驻上海总领事馆，
上海。
1929年3月14日。

亲爱的阿勒斯（Alers）：

关于您1929年3月6日的第 I.O.D 81号备忘录，我已通过电报向印度查询了雅罗斯拉夫·福尔曼内克的情况，并刚收到回复，大意是该人和卡雷尔·图尔卡，奥地利籍捷克斯洛伐克人，于1928年5月向布拉格的护照管制官申请前往印度的签证。他们自称是拳击手和记者，代表布拉格的新闻服务社、布拉哥出版的一份每周画报以及一份名为《拳台》（Ring）的体育报纸。由于对他们没有任何不良记录，因此对其签发签证未提出异议。他们于1928年9月15日抵达孟买，并称正在环球旅行。在孟买，他们通过进行拳击表演维持生计。印度方面正在进行进一步查询，结果将通知您。

此致，
G. H. A. Hall

R. C. Alers 先生，
助理警务处长，
刑事侦缉处，
上海公共租界工部局警务处，
上海。
